Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish and dust the top with more cinnamon.
Bake for 45 minutes.
hints: Matzo farfel is available in the Passover-product aisle in your supermarket. It is coarsely crumbled matzo.

title: Cranberry Rice Pilaf
description: DaVita dietitian Usha invites you to enjoy this sweet twist on regular rice pilaf, kidney-friendly recipe for Cranberry Rice Pilaf. Makes a great side dish.
steps: Soak rice and all ingredients for 40-45 minutes at room temperature.
Place all ingredients in a rice cooker.
If using a microwave rice cooker, microwave for 12 minutes at full power. If cooking stove top, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Cook covered for 20 minutes.
Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.
hints: Black cumin is a spice used in Indian and Pakistani cuisine. Look for Kala Jeera or black cumin in any Indian spice store or Asian market. It is also available online.
Select a cinnamon stick approximately 1” in length.

title: Layered Vanilla Pudding Dessert
description: Homemade crust topped with cream cheese filling, plus a layer of pudding and whipped cream make this a creamy vanilla dessert.
ingredients: 1/2 cup trans=fat free unsalted margarine or butter
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Set margarine, cream cheese and whipped topping to soften.
Combine flour and margarine, and press into a 9 x 13-inch pan. (Do not grease or spray pan with nonstick spray.)
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until crust starts to brown. Cool for 10 minutes.
Combine cream cheese, sugar and half of the whipped topping in a bowl and blend until smooth. Spread over cooled crust.
In a small bowl combine pudding and vanilla extract. Spread pudding over cream cheese mixture.
Top with remaining whipped topping. Sprinkle coconut on top. Refrigerate for 30 minutes before serving. Cut into 15 servings. Enjoy!
hints: Ready-to-eat pudding is lower in phosphorus and sodium compared to the cook and serve or instant pudding mix. Snack Pack Pudding® brand ready-to-eat vanilla pudding does not contain phosphate additives, however it is high in calcium, so avoid if you are on a low calcium diet.
Use four 3.25 ounce containers, (1 package) of ready-made pudding.
Try different flavors of pudding for a variety of tastes.
Substitute Splenda® or other low calorie sweetener for sugar to reduce carbohydrate to 19 grams per serving (one carbohydrate choice).

title: Blueberry Icebox Cake
description: Make a special kidney-friendly treat with Blueberry Icebox Cake. High in flavor and calories for those who need extra, this low potassium dessert is a keeper for your dialysis recipe collection!
steps: Preheat oven 350° F. Set butter and cream cheese out to soften.
Mix butter with flour and 2 tablespoons sugar. Press evenly into the bottom of a 9″ x 13″ x 2″ oven proof, glass baking dish. Bake for 15 minutes or until lightly browned. Remove from oven and cool.
In a large bowl, mix cream cheese with a hand mixer until smooth and fluffy. Mix in remaining sugar. Fold whipped topping into cream cheese mixture.
Spread half of the cream cheese mixture evenly over cooled crust.
Spread blueberry pie filling evenly over cream cheese mixture. Spread the remaining cream cheese mixture evenly over blueberries. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Cut into 10 servings.
hints: Not suitable for people with diabetes due to high calorie, fat and carbohydrate content.
This special company recipe can be served occasionally with a low-fat entree.

title: Salt-free Cajun Seasoning
description: Some like it hot! With Salt-free Cajun Seasoning from Ken in Lousiana you can season to your liking without worrying about getting too much sodium. Unlike some of the commercial low-sodium seasonings, Salt-free Cajun Seasoning is also potassium chloride free, keeping it low in potassium as well as sodium.
steps: Mix all ingredients together.
Store in an airtight container.
Add to any savory dish that needs more heat and spice.
hints: Regular Cajun seasoning with salt contains over 1000 mg sodium per teaspoon.
Use Salt-free Cajun Seasoning for the DaVita.com Shrimp Brouillette recipe.

title: Michigan Cherry Oat Bars
description: The best cherries are grown in the Great Lake State, and what’s better than a crunchy, sweet cherry dessert recipe to show our appreciation? Try DaVita dietitian Tara’s Michigan Cherry Oat Bars. You can use fresh of frozen cherries for this dessert.
ingredients: 2 cups fresh or frozen pitted sweet cherries
steps: Set butter out to soften.

To make cherry filling, mix the cherries, granulated sugar, corn starch and lemon juice in a sauce pan and bring to a boil over medium heat. Boil for 10 minutes or until thickened, stirring frequently. Once thickened, remove from heat and let cool to room temperature. Put in a covered bowl and refrigerate until ready to use.
Preheat oven to 350° F and spray a 9 x 9-inch square baking dish with nonstick spray. You can then line the bottom of the dish with parchment paper to make it easier to remove the bars.
Combine flour, oats, brown sugar, baking powder and salt into a bowl and mix to combine.
Add softened butter and use a pastry blender or your hands to work the mixture into crumbs.

Add 2/3 of the crumb mixture to the prepared pan and press down firmly. Top with cooled cherry filling. Sprinkle remaining crumb mixture on top of the cherries. Place in oven and bake for 30 to 35 minutes or until just golden brown.
Remove from oven and let cool completely before cutting into bars. Enjoy!
hints: You can make the filling ahead and refrigerate up to 2 days before making bars.

Bars are delicious both at room temperature or chilled in the fridge. This recipe is not recommended for people with diabetes due to the high carbohydrate content. However, it can be made with low-calorie sweeteners to decrease carbohydrate to 25 grams.

title: Turkey and Beef Meatballs
description: Serve Turkey and Beef Meatballs right out of the oven or add your favorite kidney-friendly sauce.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Mrs. Dash® Onion and Herb seasoning blend
1 cup freshly grated soft bread crumbs
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Line 2 baking sheets with foil or parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef and turkey with dry ingredients; set aside.
In a separate bowl, combine the broth, egg and Worcestershire sauce.
Add the wet ingredients to the meat mixture and mix well.
Roll into 1″ meatballs and place on baking sheets.
Bake at 30 minutes turning once halfway through baking.
Eat meatballs plain or top with your favorite kidney-friendly sauce.
hints: Make ahead and freeze for a quick meal later.
Compare sodium on broth and buy the lower sodium brand. Avoid broth that contains potassium chloride.

title: Lemony Rice Pilaf
description: Try this delicious and kidney-friendly recipe for Lemony Rice Pilaf by DaVita dietitian Brenda from Washington. She uses some of her favorite regional foods so you can create a delicious, dialysis-appropriate meal with splendid flavors from the Pacific Northwest.
ingredients: 2 cups long grain white rice, uncooked
steps: Preheat oven to 350º F. Chop the onion and mince the parsley and garlic.
In a Dutch oven melt butter over medium heat. Add the rice and stir to toast, about 4 minutes. Add the onion and garlic and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add the lemon juice, parsley and seasonings to the rice. Mix well.
Heat chicken broth to a boil and add to rice mixture. Stir well. Cover with a lid, and place in pre-heated oven. Bake for 20 minutes.
Remove rice from the oven and fluff with two forks and stir in Parmesan cheese. Garnish with parsley sprigs before serving.
hints: In step #5, if broth is not boiling, the end product will be heavy and will stick to the pan.

title: Clam Omelet
description: Clam Omelet is a family recipe shared by DaVita dietitian Amy. It is a very typical Taiwanese breakfast dish.
steps: Crack eggs in bowl and use whisk or fork to beat.
Add clams and cornstarch. Stir.
On low heat, warm oil in pan. Add mixture.
Cook on low heat until eggs are no longer runny.
Remove from heat and top each portion with 1/2 tablespoon sweet & sour sauce.
hints: This is a very typical Taiwanese dish. Amy received the recipe from her mom.

title: Golden Baked Halibut
description: Golden Baked Halibut from DaVita dietitian Elizabeth is a Middle Eastern dish baked with a creamy, fluffy sauce on top to keep the fish moist and add flavor
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F.
Place bread crumbs in a shallow dish or plate. Dredge fish fillets in bread crumbs to coat. Place in a greased shallow baking dish.
Combine mayonnaise and lemon juice. Add yogurt and blend well.
In a separate bowl, beat egg white until stiff, then gently fold into mayonnaise mixture.
Sprinkle chopped green onion over fillets. Spoon mayonnaise mixture over top. Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake for 20-25 minutes or until fish flakes easily.
hints: This recipe works well with snapper or cod.
Adjust portion to match your meal plan and protein goals.
Sour cream may be substituted for yogurt. Potassium and phosphorus are slightly lower but fat is higher.

title: Party Punch
description: Nothing says party like the kidney-friendly recipe for Party Punch (low sugar).
ingredients: 1 pint sherbet lemon or lime flavor
steps: Place soda in a punch bowl or a large mixing bowl.
Add fruit punch concentrate and stir.
With an ice cream scoop add sherbet.
When sherbet starts to melt stir and serve.
hints: Look for frozen fruit punch concentrate, not fruit punch juice.
Fruit punch already made in jugs, boxes or cartons generally has added phosphorus. Which is why frozen fruit punch concentrate is recommended.

title: Pineapple-Mint Flavored Water
description: Water is one of the healthiest beverages for kidney patients–but nobody says it has to be plain and tasteless! Try Pineapple-Mint Flavored Water, one of many flavored water recipes from DaVita dietitian Kara.
steps: Dice pineapple.
Chop mint leaves.
Add all ingredients to a pitcher.
Refrigerator overnight before serving.
hints: If you are on limited fluids, adjust the portion size to meet your needs.
After flavors develop you can pour into ice cube trays to make flavored ice.

title: Honey Spice-Rubbed Salmon
description: Try a tasty Honey Spice-Rubbed Salmon for dinner and you’ll want to have it again for lunch the next day. This flavorful and kidney-friendly recipe is easy to prepare in the oven or on the grill.
steps: Place honey, grated lemon peel, ground pepper, garlic powder and hot water in a small bowl and whisk until blended. With gloved hands, rub mixture over salmon fillets.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add spice-rubbed salmon fillets and cook 4 minutes. Carefully turn fillets with a spatula.
Reduce heat to medium-low and cook an additional 4 to 6 minutes, until fish turns opaque throughout and flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Arrange 1/2-cup arugula on each plate. Place salmon fillet on top of arugula and serve.
hints: Purchase 4 salmon fillets, 4 ounces each.
Serve with Cucumber Dill Salsa.
Cook the salmon fillets on an outdoor grill if desired.
For a low-protein diet, adjust portion according to your meal plan or consult with your dietitian.

title: Chinese Five Spice
description: One of the unique qualities of the United States is the mixture of worldwide cultures. It provides an opportunity to discover delicious flavors of other countries and share them with friends. Tahseen, a DaVita renal dietitian from Florida, has lived all over the world and experienced a variety of tasty food. Today she shares her kidney-friendly recipes for Chinese Five Spice from China.
steps: Grind all spices and keep in an airtight container until ready to use in a recipe.
hints: Chinese Five Spice is popular in Chinese cooking and many Asian dishes.
Use Chinese Five Spice in egg rolls, Chinese bok choy soup or roast chicken drumsticks.
Sichuan peppercorns are also known as Szechuan peppercorns.

title: Everyday Cake
description: Suzette, a DaVita renal dietitian from Louisiana, is willing to share one of her family’s best kept secrets — the recipe to her grandmother’s Everyday Cake. Modified to be dialysis and diabetes friendly, this simple cake packs a mouthful of flavor in each bite.
ingredients: 1/3 cup Splenda® No Calorie sweetener granulated
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Mix Splenda®, 1 cup flour and nutmeg.
Add milk, egg and applesauce. Mix well.
Pour batter into a 9” x 9” greased baking dish.
In a small bowl mix 1/4 cup flour, cinnamon, brown sugar Splenda® and melted margarine.
Spoon topping over batter.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden brown.
hints: Substitute unenriched rice milk for low-fat milk if desired.
Self-rising flour contains salt and baking powder. To make your own add 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1-1/2 teaspoon baking powder to each cup of all purpose flour.

title: Omelet with Summer Vegetables
description: Vegetables are delicious during the summertime, and even more delicious when placed into the kidney-friendly omelet, Omelet with Summer Vegetables.
ingredients: 1/4 cup frozen whole kernel corn, thawed
1/4 teaspoon Extra Spicy Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
1 ounce low fat sharp cheddar cheese, shredded
steps: Heat a small saucepan over medium-high heat. Coat pan with cooking spray. Add corn, zucchini and onions to pan; sauté 4 minutes or until vegetables are crisp-tender. Remove from heat.
Heat a 10” nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Combine water, pepper (or Mrs. Dash®), egg whites and egg in a bowl, stirring well with a whisk.

Coat pan with cooking spray. Pour egg mixture into pan; cook until edges begin to set (about 2 minutes). Gently lift the edges of the omelet with a spatula, tilting the pan to allow uncooked egg mixture to come into contact with the pan.

Spoon vegetable mixture onto half of omelet, sprinkle cheese over vegetable mixture. Loosen omelet with a spatula and fold in half. Cook 2 minutes more or until cheese melts. Carefully slide omelet onto a plate.
hints: Substitute any variety of Mrs, Dash seasoning or black pepper if you do not like spicy seasonong.

For those following a CKD non-dialysis diet: This higher protein recipe may be appropriate for your diet if the portion size were adjusted to reduce protein content. Adjustments should be based on your individual protein prescription. Check with your dietitian if you are unsure.

title: Crock-Pot® Chicken and White Bean Chili
description: Imagine coming home to a ready-to eat, homemade dish of chili on the next cool winter’s eve. DaVita dietitian Deanna’s recipe for Crock-Pot® Chicken and White Bean Chili is perfect for a fix-it-and-forget-it meal.
steps: Cut chicken breast in bite sized cubes. Season with black pepper and place in Crock-Pot.
Dice carrots, celery and onion (except pearl onions). Mince garlic. Rinse and drain beans and hominy to reduce sodium.
Add chicken broth, beans, hominy, pearl onions, diced onion, carrots, celery, garlic and green chilies to Crock-Pot.
Season with garlic powder, cumin, chili powder, oregano and cayenne pepper.
Cover with lid and cook on low setting for 8 hours. Serve hot.
hints: Adjust the amount of chicken for a lower or higher protein diet.
This is a higher potassium dish. Check with your dietitian before trying it if you have high potassium levels or if you are on a low potassium diet.
Omit beans for a lower potassium and phosphorus version of this recipe (555 mg potassium, 202 mg phosphorus).

title: Roasted Garlic Heads
description: So many recipes call for garlic–why not roast several heads to have soft, caramelized garlic ready to use? This Roasted Garlic Heads recipe is kidney-friendly and versatile to use in recipes, as a spread, in dips or dressings. The roasted cloves will keep in the refrigerator for 1 week or can be frozen up to 3 months.
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F.
Remove the outer papery skin of garlic heads, leaving the cloves intact.
Cut the top 1/4-inch off garlic heads to expose the cloves.

In a small baking dish place heads with cut side up. Pour oil over garlic heads. Cover with foil and bake for 45 to 60 minutes or until cloves are soft. Let cool, then pull or squeeze garlic cloves from the skins.
hints: Add roasted garlic to recipes, spread on toasted bread, or stir into sour cream or Greek yogurt to make a dip.
Store unused garlic in the refrigerator or freezer.

title: Pumpkin Cookies
description: Pumpkin Cookies have just enough pumpkin for flavor without making the potassium too high. Bake a batch to kick off the holidays with the sweet smell of ginger and cinnamon.
ingredients: 1/2 cup canned pumpkin (not pumpkin pie filling)
steps: Set the butter out to soften. Preheat oven to 350° F.
Mix the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, cloves, allspice and salt in large bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and brown sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer on medium-speed until light and fluffy.
Add the pumpkin, egg and vanilla; beat well. Gradually beat in the flour mixture on low speed until well mixed.
Using about a tablespoon form dough into balls. Roll in granulated sugar. Place 2 inches apart on an ungreased baking sheets and press gently with a fork to flatten slightly.

Bake 8 to 10 minutes or until edges of cookies just begin to brown. If desired, after removing baking sheet from the oven, immediately press 3 to 4 white chocolate chips into the center of each cookie. Remove to wire racks and cool completely.
Store cookies in airtight container up to 5 days.
hints: Dark chocolate or semi-chocolate whips work well in this recipe.
Without the white chocolate chips carbohydrate content is 18 grams per serving.

title: Low Potassium Style Stewed Potatoes
description: For your next dinner side dish, try the kidney-friendly recipe for Low Potassium Style Stewed Potatoes.
steps: Dice potatoes into 1/2-inch cubes and soak or double-boil to reduce potassium if you are on a low potassium diet. (See details in helpful hints).
Place potatoes in a saucepan with 4 cups water and boil over medium heat for 15 minutes or until cooked.
Drain potatoes, discard water and return to pan. Add 1/2 cup hot water, nondairy creamer, garlic or onion powder, pepper and margarine. Heat to a boil.
Combine 2 teaspoons flour in a tablespoon of cold tap water. Stir into potatoes and continue stirring until liquid thickens.
hints: Potatoes are very high in potassium but you can remove part of the potassium by using one of these methods:

Double cook method: Peel and dice potatoes. Place in a large pot of water and bring to a boil. Drain the water and add fresh water to the pot. Bring to a boil, cook for 10 minutes then drain and set aside.
Leaching method: Peel and dice potatoes. Place in a large pot of warm tap water and soak for 2 to 4 hours. Drain and set aside.
Add a little water if sauce thickens too much.

title: Zesty Barbecue Sauce
description: Add some zest to your chicken or beef with this kidney-friendly recipe for Zesty Barbeque Sauce.
steps: Finely chop onion.
Combine vinegars, water, black pepper, ketchup, chili powder, onion and Tabasco sauce.
Add seasonings: poultry seasoning, dry mustard, onion powder, garlic powder, ginger, ginger ale and lemon juice.
Add brown sugar and Liquid Smoke.
In a separate container, mix flour and oil to make a paste until all lumps of flour have disappeared. Add paste to sauce.
Cook for 15 minutes on low heat.
Pour or brush on baked or grilled meats.
hints: Use on hamburgers, beef ribs, chicken, short ribs and steaks.

title: Spicy Corn Bread
description: DaVita dietitian, Heather from Georgia, enjoys spending time in the kitchen coming up with delicious recipes for her dialysis patients to enjoy. One of her favorites is Spicy Corn Bread, a kidney-friendly recipe.
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F.
In large mixing bow, combine flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder, chili powder and pepper. Stir to combine.
Add rice milk, egg, egg white and oil to dry ingredients and stir just until moistened.
Gently stir scallions, carrots and garlic into cornbread mixture.
Pour batter into an 8”-square baking pan which been coated with nonstick cooking spray.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until top starts to turn golden brown. Cut into eight 2” x 4” pieces.
hints: For variation, try onion instead of scallions and red bell pepper instead of carrots.

title: Microwave Egg and Veggie Jars
description: It’s easy to assemble Microwave Egg and Veggie Jars. Store in the fridge and when you are ready for breakfast just add two eggs and microwave for a quick, healthy breakfast.
steps: In a small skillet cook the turkey sausage until browned. Chop into crumbles while cooking.
Prepare the jars by spraying the insides with cooking spray.
Dice the bell pepper, onion, broccoli and mushrooms. In a small bowl combine the chopped vegetables. Slice the jalapeno pepper.
Add 1/4 cup sausage, 1 tablespoon cheese, 1/4 cup diced vegetables mixture and 2 to 3 jalapeno pepper slices to each jar.
Cover and store the jars for up to 4 days in the refrigerator.
When ready to eat, beat 2 eggs, add to the jar and stir well. Microwave for 30 seconds and stir. Repeat until eggs are set. (It may take 1-1/2 to 2 minutes depending on your microwave.)
Carefully remove the jar from the microwave and enjoy.
hints: • The jars can be frozen. Transfer from the freezer to the refrigerator the night before you plan to add eggs and cook. • Mix and match other lower potassium vegetables such as asparagus, green onion, kale or zucchini. • Select a natural low-sodium cheese like cheddar or Swiss. If using a higher sodium cheese like parmesan or feta reduce the amount to 1/2 tablespoon •Choose from chicken or turkey sausage without phosphorus additives. Be aware some reduced-sodium breakfast meats are quite high in potassium due to potassium additives. • For an additive-free, lower sodium sausage try Homemade Turkey Sausage or Homemade Pan Sausage from recipes on DaVita.com.

title: Southern Style Stuffed Peppers
description: Southern Style Stuffed Peppers have all the ingredients for a complete meal plus a double dose of nutritious vegetables that fit into a kidney-friendly diet.
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F.
Core and de-seed bell peppers.
Brown ground beef and drain liquid.
Add onion, rice, garlic powder, black pepper, parsley and tomato sauce to cooked beef; simmer for 10 minutes.
Fill each bell pepper with mixture.
Bake for 1 hour.
hints: Freeze extra servings for a quick meal later.

title: Baked Blueberry-Peach Oatmeal
description: Baked Blueberry-Peach Oatmeal combines cinnamon, vanilla and almond milk with oats and fruit for a delightful hot breakfast. Freeze the extra portions for a quick meal throughout the week.
ingredients: 1 cup diced peaches, fresh, canned or frozen
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F and prepare an 8 x 8-inch baking pan by greasing with butter or cooking spray.
Melt the butter.
In a large bowl mix together oats, almond milk, eggs, brown sugar, butter, baking powder, vanilla and cinnamon. Add the blueberries and undrained diced peaches and stir to combine.
Spread mixture evenly into the prepared baking dish and bake for 30 to 40 minutes until set.
Cool slightly. Cut into squares and serve warm.
hints: Baked squares can be frozen for a quick and easy breakfast. Heat in the microwave for a minute or until heated.
For a low sugar version replace brown sugar with low-calorie sweetener and use fresh peaches. Carbohydrates are reduced to 24 grams per serving.
